focal_entities.audience: the user at the goal sign-off, approving what the finished work will do and why, and rn's orchestrator in any later conversation, carrying the work on without asking them again

goal_orientation.purpose: approving the goal and the acceptance criteria, then carrying each later work to them

constraints.decision: Purpose: Files pile up in the Downloads folder and the user cannot find the one they want; the tool sorts them by type (such as images, documents, archives) into groups so they are easy to find.
Where sorted files go: Files are moved into one folder per type (such as Images, Documents, Archives) made inside the Downloads folder itself; no folder outside Downloads is touched.
Operating systems: The tool works on macOS and Linux; Windows is not needed.

Safety: Run plainly, the tool only lists which file would move to which folder and moves nothing; it moves files only when the user explicitly tells it to. It never deletes, renames or overwrites any file. No undo is provided; the user moves files back by hand.

Same name at the destination: When the destination folder already holds a file of the same name, that file is left where it is and the list shows it is not moved because of the same name; the other files are still moved.

Types: Files are told apart by their extension and sorted into a fixed set of types: Images, Documents, Archives, Audio, Video and Installers (such as .dmg and .deb); no settings are needed or offered.

Files of no type, folders and hidden files: Files with no extension or an extension of none of the six types, folders already in Downloads, and hidden files (such as .DS_Store) are all left where they are; the list shows each file of no type as not moved.
Folder to organize: With no folder given the tool organizes ~/Downloads; given a folder, it organizes that folder instead.

What shows it done: Done when all of these hold on both macOS and Linux: on a trial folder holding files of all six types, files of no type, existing folders, hidden files and a same-name clash, a plain run prints the correct list and moves no file; a run told to move moves files as listed, and no file is lost, renamed or overwritten; the README says how to install the tool and how to use it; and tests check the behaviour above. The user does not check it on their own Downloads.

UX document: A UX document of kind ux is made at .rn/20261030-organize-downloads-cli/ux.md, kept in the session folder alone and not left in the repository, for the user to approve and the README and the tool to be built from.

README: The repository's README.md, a document of kind readme, is changed into the tool's README, so whoever opens the repository reads how to install and use it at once; the repository's one-line playground description stays at its top.
